The delete card description mentions pausing the old ad, suggesting promoted posts can be paused.

Promoted posts have no entity status of their own, so pausing losers requires pausing the line item directly. Splitting campaigns by country is better than combining them: Ireland has higher intent but a smaller audience, while the UK offers cheaper reach but lower relevance. Keeping them separate prevents the UK from overwhelming impressions and starving the home market.

A single campaign with four line items is cleaner than separate campaigns. Each line item will carry one creative only, since pausing a line item pauses all creatives on it.

Six line items would fragment the daily budget too thin for reliable learning. A phased rollout is better: test three creatives across both geos in the first two days to find the cheapest link clicks, then pause losers and shift budget to the winner. Splitting that winner into separate Ireland and UK line items may be necessary, but the current metric groups might not provide a geo breakdown.

Account stats probably lack geo breakdowns, so separate line items are needed from the start. The revised plan uses two line items by country, each carrying the top two or three creatives. The algorithm will naturally favor stronger creatives within each ad group. One downside remains: a poor creative cannot be paused individually if it is on a shared line item.

Three line items by creative will target both countries. This lets me pause weak creatives individually, though UK impressions may dominate delivery. The posts differ significantly in quality, so creative testing is more valuable than a geo split. English is the chosen language.

The language restriction will be broadened to include all languages within Ireland and the UK. English copy is readable by many Irish speakers, and excluding non-English users would be unnecessary.

Age targeting will remain unset. The Halloween and ghost song theme may appeal to older listeners, but leaving it open maximizes reach for anyone who can stream.

Interest stacking would reduce reach and raise CPM, so a hybrid targeting strategy is better. A broad line item for Ireland will use the strongest copy to capture high intent. A separate interest-targeted line item for the UK will target folk, Irish culture, Halloween, and classical music. The available interest categories still need to be checked.

The plan is now three broad line items across Ireland and the UK, using the three creatives directly without interest targeting. The first will use "Press play before the 31st," the second "Free," and the third "plastic pumpkins." The budget will be spent fully each day to maximize link clicks.

The campaign end time is set to 1 November at midnight Dublin time. This avoids cutting off the last hour of the campaign due to the October 31 daylight saving change.

The campaign will use promoted tweets with link clicks as the goal and website clicks as the objective. Audience expansion is set to defined so only eligible listeners are reached. Auto bidding and standard delivery will be used across all placements. The funding instrument is yby3ct. I will create the campaign first, then add the three line items.

A fourth creative was considered but rejected. The descriptive post is too similar to the existing factual posts, and the weak "Hope you enjoy it" post will not be promoted. The implementation plan now has seven steps: create the campaign, add three line items with Ireland and UK location targeting, promote the posts, activate everything, and verify the status.

I will wait until tomorrow to schedule the campaign. I am avoiding language and age targeting to prevent API errors from incorrect values. I also need to check whether WEBSITE_CLICKS requires an advertiser domain.

The advertiser domain requirement does not apply because placements are set to ALL_ON_TWITTER. LINK_CLICKS is the correct goal for a WEBSITE_CLICKS objective, since SITE_VISITS would require a universal website tag.
